strategies.name: liquidity_grab_reversal
strategies.entry_summary: Look for a liquidity grab: price breaks support or resistance, makes a fakeout, and then reverses in the opposite direction. Enter at the candle that made the liquidity grab; for longs, the entry is at the candle that broke support, and for shorts, the entry is at the candle that made the resistance
strategies.exit_summary: Place the stop loss just beyond the liquidity grab, and take profit at a recent swing high for longs or recent swing low for shorts. The video also frames the trade as a reversal at the top or bottom of the move, with higher-timeframe support/resistance used as a confluence filter in one variant.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter at the candle that initiated the liquidity grab
variants.target_note: take profit at a recent high/low
variants.transcript_quote: your entry would be at the candle that made the liquidity grab

variants.timeframe_note: not specified; same setup with added oscillator confirmation
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: combine the liquidity grab with momentum divergence confirmation
variants.target_note: same stop/target structure; profit from the reversal after confluence
variants.transcript_quote: we combine both the powers of the Divergence and the bullish liquidity grab

strategies.name: higher_timeframe_liquidity_grab_reversal_filter
strategies.entry_summary: On a lower timeframe, take a liquidity-grab reversal only when the signal occurs at a higher-timeframe support or resistance level. The example uses a 15-minute signal checked against a 1-hour chart and only takes the trade when the lower-timeframe reversal aligns with the higher-timeframe level.
strategies.exit_summary: Use the normal liquidity-grab stop loss below/above the grab and take profit at the recent swing high/low on the lower timeframe. Do not take the trade if the higher-timeframe context shows the move is in the middle of a range rather than at an extreme.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: require the lower-timeframe liquidity grab to occur at higher-timeframe support/resistance
variants.target_note: normal 15m stop loss and take profit structure
variants.transcript_quote: we then move to a 1hour time frame and we see this Buy Signal signal happened exactly at a support on a higher time frame

result.enumeration_note: Two distinct skeletons are taught: the base liquidity-grab reversal, and a separate higher-timeframe support/resistance filter for taking only extremes; divergence is a compatible confluence variant of the base setup.
